title: Accounts Receivable Standing Rules for Hardware Procurement Invoices
content:
1. **Due dates.** Hardware Procurement deposits are due on receipt; other invoices fall due the order type's invoice terms in calendar days after posting.
2. **Applying payments.** A payment is applied to the invoice its remittance names; otherwise to the oldest open invoice of the order first. One ledger entry is made per invoice applied.
3. **Card payments.** Card payments are accepted only for an invoice whose total does not exceed the order type's card limit.
4. **Late fees.** On the first day of each calendar month, every invoice still unpaid more than the order type's grace days after its due date is assessed one late fee of the monthly late fee percentage of its unpaid balance, or the order type's minimum late fee if greater, rounded half up to the cent.

### Late fee, worked (hypothetical figures)

| Unpaid balance | Monthly percentage | Percentage amount | Minimum | Late fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000.00 | 1.5 | 15.00 | 25.00 | 25.00 (the minimum is greater) |
| 4000.00 | 1.5 | 60.00 | 35.00 | 60.00 |
| 2345.67 | 1.5 | 35.18505 | 25.00 | 35.19 |

### Grace, worked (abstract)

With a grace of 5 days, an invoice whose due date fell 5 days before the first of the month is not more than 5 days past due on that first and is not assessed that month; one whose due date fell 6 days before is assessed.

### Applying a payment without a named invoice (hypothetical)

An order carries two open invoices, posted in March and in May. A remittance naming neither is applied to the March invoice first.
